findings.finding: The key risk and the bear story are not in the numbers: in all three scenarios the engine's FY2027 capex (maintenance + growth capex) drops to about 84B (bear 26.8+57.1), 97.5B (base 28.5+69.0) and 104B (bull 29.9+74.3), a 25-40% cut from the guided 135-145B of 2026 (9M 2026 purchases of property and equipment 83.06B, 10-Q 2026-10-22). Nothing in the evidence supports a cut: the 2027 capex outlook comes only at the Q4 call, non-cancelable commitments due 2027 are 121.41B and 355.73B of leases not yet commenced start through 2036. The bear event explicitly says capex keeps rising in 2027 while the bear drivers cut it the most (sales_to_capital 0.55 on smaller revenue growth). The model's what_must_be_true confirms the blind spot: the capital_efficiency lever is not_reachable (value stays 861-1,063 across 0-6x growth investment), so the decisive risk the table names cannot move the fair value of 875.
findings.where: companies/META/out/casefile.json val.case.scenarios[bear|base|bull].periods[2027-12-31] maintenance_capex/growth_capex; position/core.json drivers sales_to_capital per scenario; casefile val.what_must_be_true lever capital_efficiency; position/core.json bear event on capex
findings.fix: Repair: set FY2027 (and FY2028) capex per scenario from company evidence (at least the 2026 level 135-145B in bear, a reasoned path in base, citing dc_g_capex_fy2026 and the 10-Q commitment schedule) via a capex/reinvestment override or lower near-year sales_to_capital, rerun ticker-value, and check that the fair value responds; if the engine lever cannot carry it, state the 2027 capex assumption next to the table as a visible gap.

findings.finding: Counter-thesis (pre-mortem, November 2029: the investment failed): Meta spent 140B+ a year on AI infrastructure through 2028 while ad impressions growth fell from 19% to near zero and price-per-ad gains faded as competitors' AI ad tools (Google, Amazon, TikTok) caught up; incremental ROIC, already 14.9% against 28.7% on the legacy base (prefetch/forensic.json), sank toward the cost of capital; D&A from the 2025-2027 build (9M 2026 D&A 19.5B, rising each quarter) pushed the margin after SBC toward the 2022 level (about 25%); the 60B ATM and youth/EU legal costs diluted holders; the market re-rated the stock from a compounder to a utility-like capex spender. Early signs: impressions growth below 5% for two quarters, 2027 capex guide above 150B with no Muse/business-AI revenue disclosed, quarterly FCF negative again, ATM sales reported in a 10-Q, incremental ROIC below 12% on FY2026 data.
findings.fix: Carry these early signs as dated numeric falsifiers/monitors in the bear (impressions growth, capex guide, ATM usage, FCF) and show the counter-thesis next to the result.

findings.finding: The bear does not really break the business; its price comes from the multiple. Bear revenue still grows 13% (FY2027 289B) and 8-11% after, margin after SBC 32.9% -> 30.0%, above Meta's own 2022 trough (~25%) and with no explicit legal, EU or D&A drag, and no equity issuance. The year-1 bear price 350$ (-43%) is mostly a forward P/E of 10.5x (roic 0.1) on EPS only 10% below base (31.3 vs 34.7). Year-1 EPS spread across scenarios is about +-10% while prices span 350-1,402 (forward P/E 10.5x / 21.2x / 34.1x): close to the guardrail 'one EPS path x three multiples'.
findings.where: position/core.json bear drivers (growth_anchor 0.13, mature_margin 0.3); casefile company_path.scenarios.*.rows year 0-1 eps/multiple
findings.fix: Size the bear mechanisms in the drivers: margin toward the evidenced 2022 trough or below via D&A ramp and recurring legal costs (2.4B + 9.89B charges in 2026, 5.3B contingent AG amount), the EU share (about 22% of Q3 revenue) at risk, the ATM dilution; then let the economics multiple follow, so the bear differs in EPS, not only in multiple.

findings.finding: Funding and dilution are in the events but not in the model: weighted shares are constant at 2,556.24M in every year of every scenario and equity_proceeds = 0 / financing_status none in every period. The bear event says the ~60B ATM is used (at bear prices of ~350-450$ that is roughly 130-170M shares, 5-7% dilution); the base event says the 40M-share forward sale (24.9B) settles by November 2027. Neither the shares nor the cash appear.
findings.where: casefile company_path.fiscal_years.*.weighted_shares; val.case.scenarios[*].periods[*].equity_proceeds; position/core.json bear and base events on equity
findings.fix: Model the forward settlement in base (40M shares, 24.9B cash) and the ATM in bear (equity_proceeds with issue price at the bear path), or remove the events from the scenario reasons; rerun ticker-value.

findings.finding: Capital bridge asymmetry: the 6.50% mandatory convertible preferred is added as a 12.5B debt-like claim, but its 12.46B net cash proceeds (received 2026-10-29, after the 2026-09-30 balance sheet) are explicitly not in the opening cash. A post-statement financing must enter both sides; as entered it lowers value by about 4.9$/share. The open item 'opening_vs_validated_data' (debt 116.05B = 83.67B + 32.38B reclassification) is still waiting for acceptance.
findings.where: companies/META/inputs.json forecast.debt_like_claims[kind preferred_or_minority]; casefile val.case.opening unrestricted_cash / debt; casefile rv.open_items
findings.fix: Add the 12.46B net proceeds to opening cash (or marketable investments) with the dc_8k_20261029 evidence, or net the claim; keep the litigation 19.88B claim; record the reviewer acceptance of the reclassification.

findings.finding: Bull multiple not justified by the company's own return record: bull rests on roic 0.30 for 13 explicit years plus terminal (forward P/E 34.1x in year 0, 29.6x in year 1), labelled justified_high. Meta's ROIC was 28.7% in FY2025 and the incremental ROIC on the AI build is 14.9% (prefetch/forensic.json); 30% equals the legacy average only. 34x is near the top of own_history (high 39.1, median 27.1) and the year-1 bull +128% depends on it. The own_history median 27.1x forward P/E also looks high for 2022-2026 (today's price is ~17.7x base FY2027 EPS) and should be checked against its source (nm_ib_history).
findings.where: casefile company_path.scenarios.bull (roic 0.3, justification justified_high, multiple_path); company_path.own_history
findings.fix: Relabel bull as unproven (or peak) unless evidence shows the new capital earning ~30%; consider roic 0.25 tied to the 2023-2025 record; verify own_history low/median/high against the saved price and EPS series.

findings.finding: Unsized exposures and screens: Asia-Pacific is about 26% of revenue with the China-based reseller share undisclosed, and chip/server supplier and Taiwan/export-control exposure are undisclosed (gather/macro.json gaps); neither is a bear mechanism or a risk row. Beneish is unavailable (prefetch/forensic.json), so the earnings-manipulation screen is a gap, not a pass.
findings.where: gather/macro.json gaps; prefetch/forensic.json beneish; position/core.json bear events
findings.fix: Name the China-advertiser and AI-supply-chain exposures as unsized risks (hypothesis) next to the result and state the Beneish gap.

findings.finding: Falsifiers miss the thesis-critical metrics: the bull's central claims (margin back to 42%, AI products earning money in 2027, no ATM) have only a revenue falsifier; no scenario has a capex or ROIC/FCF falsifier although the key risk is capex outrunning cash flow.
findings.fix: Add e.g. operating margin FY2027 below 0.36 by 2028-02-15 (bull), capex FY2027 above 160B with revenue growth below 18% (base/bear), ATM shares sold > 0 by 2027-11-15 (bull).
